To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

EBA in the omission failure model is equivalent to continual common knowledge among the processors, and EBA in the crash failure model is equivalent in a certain sense to a variant of continual common knowledge among processors that do not fail.

(a) continual common knowledge is necessary and sufficient for EBA; (b) continual common knowledge can be characterized in a way that is very similar to the characterization of common knowledge for SBA; (c) optimal EBA protocols can be constructed from any given EBA protocol using our technique.

(1) common knowledge is a necessary and a sufficient condition for SBA; (2) continual common knowledge is a sufficient and necessary condition for EBA; (3) the optimal EBA protocols are the ones that use continual common knowledge; (4) the optimal EDA protocols can be obtained by applying a certain transformation to any EBA protocol; and (5) the optimal EDBA protocols can be obtained in a similar fashion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (a) What is the state of knowledge required by processors in order to achieve EBA?
a characterization of the states of common knowledge required for attaining E BA.
the characterization of EBA protocols and the development of a construction technique that allows us, given any EBA protocol with certain properties, to arrive at an optimal one.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
optimal EBA in the crash model is characterized by continual common knowledge and optimal EBA in omission model is characterized by common knowledge.

the optimal EBA protocol in the crash model is the same as the optimal SBA protocol in the same model, while the optimal EBA protocols for the omission failure models are the same as optimal SBA protocols for the same models.
EBA can be attained in the crash and the omission models if and only if continual common knowledge exists.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBA can be characterized in terms of continual common knowledge, and optimal EBA can be constructed from an arbitrary EBA protocol.
the state of continual knowledge of the nonfaulty processes is a necessary and a sufficient condition for attaning EBA.
we provide an alternative characterization of EBA in the crash and the omission models, and we also provide a technique that can be used to transform an EBA protocol into an optimal protocol.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the characterization of optimal EBA protocols is not as straightforward as the characterization of optimal SBA protocols.
, for EBA, the knowledge of nonfaulty processors plays a much more central role than in SBA.
EBA protocols can be designed by starting with an SBA protocol, applying the construction twice, and then replacing the SBA protocol by an optimal EBA one.
